stories.title: Somali Parliamentary Delegation in Tanzania for Regional and Global Meetings
stories.description: ARUSHA — The Speaker of Somalia’s House of the People, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur (Jama), and a delegation he leads arrived in Arusha, Tanzania, on Wednesday to participate in the 21st meeting of the Bureau of Speakers of East African Community (EAC) parliaments and the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU). The delegation was received at Arusha Airport by Somalia’s Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community, Ilyas Ali Hassan, and other officials. Somalia Chairs EAC Speakers’ Bureau The 21st meeting of the EAC Speakers’ Bureau is particularly significant for Somalia, as Speaker Jama chairs the body. As detailed in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the Arusha meeting, Somalia assumed the chairmanship of the EAC Speakers’ Bureau from Kenya in November 2025, a development described as a demonstration that no single member state dominates the community. During the meeting, Speaker Jama briefed his counterparts on the progress of Somalia’s 11th Federal Parliament, highlighting achievements in state-building, the completion and ratification of the provisional constitution, security and the rule of law, public financial management, and economic development. He noted that the House of the People has approved more than 56 laws and 18 resolutions. Speaker Jama also announced that Somalia is ready to host the 22nd meeting of the Bureau of Speakers of EAC parliaments in Mogadishu at the end of January 2027. He expressed optimism that Mogadishu would welcome the Bureau and that the meeting would reinforce joint efforts toward building a united, prosperous East African Community living in lasting peace. On the sidelines of the Arusha meeting, Speaker Jama held a bilateral meeting with the Speaker of Kenya’s National Assembly, Moses Wetang’ula. The two leaders discussed strengthening parliamentary cooperation, exchanging experiences and building institutional knowledge. Both sides emphasised the role of their respective parliaments in representing the interests and […]
